description: An exploration of the meaning, categories and protection of human rights, the relationship between rights and duties, and the pursuit of social justice, equality and equity in Tanzania.

options.text: Privileges given only to wealthy citizens by the government
Basic entitlements and freedoms that belong to every person simply because they are human
Rules made only for adults who have national identity cards
Rewards earned by paying taxes to the state

mcq.explanation: Human rights are the basic entitlements and freedoms that every human being possesses from birth, regardless of status, wealth or nationality.

mcq.questionText: When human rights are said to be 'inalienable', this means that they are

options.text: Given temporarily and may be withdrawn at any time
Owned only by government officials
Cannot be taken away or surrendered, because they belong to every person
Available only to people above eighteen years of age

mcq.explanation: Inalienable means human rights cannot be taken away from a person or given up, since they are an inherent part of being human.

mcq.questionText: The characteristic of human rights which means they apply to all people everywhere without discrimination is called

options.text: Universality
Nationality
Seniority
Majority

mcq.explanation: Universality means human rights belong to all human beings everywhere, regardless of race, sex, religion or any other status.

mcq.questionText: Which international document, adopted in 1948, set out a common standard of human rights for all peoples and nations?

options.text: The Treaty of Versailles
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
The Arusha Declaration
The Berlin Conference Agreement

mcq.explanation: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1948 as a common standard of achievement for all nations.

mcq.questionText: The right to vote and the right to a fair trial are best classified as

options.text: Economic and social rights
Civil and political rights
Cultural rights
Solidarity rights

mcq.explanation: Civil and political rights protect individual freedom and participation in public life, including the right to vote and the right to a fair trial.

mcq.questionText: The rights to education, health and work belong to which category of human rights?

options.text: Civil and political rights
Group or solidarity rights
Economic, social and cultural rights
Religious rights only

mcq.explanation: Economic, social and cultural rights include the rights to education, health, work and an adequate standard of living.

mcq.questionText: The right to a clean environment and the right to development are examples of

options.text: Civil rights
Group or solidarity rights
Personal property rights
Political rights

mcq.explanation: Group or solidarity rights (third-generation rights) are enjoyed collectively and include the rights to development, peace and a clean environment.

mcq.questionText: In the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania, the section that lists the basic rights and freedoms of citizens is commonly known as the

options.text: Bill of Rights and Duties
Penal Code
Electoral Act
Land Act

mcq.explanation: The Bill of Rights and Duties was added to the Constitution of Tanzania in 1984 and guarantees basic rights and freedoms as well as fundamental duties of citizens.

mcq.questionText: Which national institution in Tanzania is responsible for promoting and protecting human rights and good governance?

options.text: The Bank of Tanzania
The Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance (CHRAGG)
The Tanzania Revenue Authority
The National Electoral Commission

mcq.explanation: CHRAGG is the national human rights institution established to promote, protect and investigate violations of human rights and principles of good governance in Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Social justice is best described as

options.text: Punishing all citizens equally for any offence
Fair distribution of resources, opportunities and privileges within a society
Giving more rights to people who hold government positions
Allowing the strongest groups to control the nation's wealth

mcq.explanation: Social justice refers to fairness in the distribution of wealth, opportunities and privileges so that all members of society are treated justly.

mcq.questionText: The difference between equality and equity is best explained by which statement?

options.text: Equality means treating everyone the same, while equity means giving each person what they need to reach a fair outcome
Equality and equity mean exactly the same thing
Equity means ignoring people's needs, while equality means favouring the rich
Equality applies only to men, while equity applies only to women

mcq.explanation: Equality treats everyone identically, while equity recognises different needs and provides support accordingly so that everyone can achieve fair results.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a fundamental DUTY of a citizen as emphasised in the Constitution of Tanzania?

options.text: To refuse to pay any taxes
To safeguard public property and obey the laws of the land
To ignore the rights of other people
To avoid participating in national development

mcq.explanation: Among the fundamental duties are safeguarding public property, obeying the law, paying taxes and participating in lawful national activities.

mcq.questionText: Which Tanzanian law is specifically aimed at protecting the rights and welfare of children?

options.text: The Law of the Child Act of 2009
The Mining Act
The Banking Act
The Wildlife Conservation Act

mcq.explanation: The Law of the Child Act, 2009 consolidates laws relating to children in Tanzania and protects their rights to care, protection and development.

mcq.questionText: A common cause of human rights violations in society is

options.text: Widespread respect for the rule of law
Ignorance of one's rights and poor enforcement of laws
Free and fair access to courts
Strong civic education programmes

mcq.explanation: Causes of violations include ignorance of rights, weak law enforcement, poverty, discrimination and abuse of power by those in authority.

mcq.questionText: The relationship between rights and responsibilities is best summarised by the statement that

options.text: Rights can be enjoyed without respecting the rights of others
Every right carries a corresponding responsibility to respect the same right in others
Responsibilities are only for the government, not citizens
Having a right removes all duties from a person

mcq.explanation: Rights and responsibilities are inseparable; enjoying your rights requires you to respect the equal rights of others and fulfil your duties to society.

fib.questionText: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations in the year _____.
fib.explanation: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948.

fib.questionText: Rights that cannot be taken away or given up because they belong to every human being are said to be _____.
fib.explanation: Inalienable is the characteristic meaning human rights cannot be surrendered or removed.

fib.questionText: The part of the Constitution of Tanzania that lists basic rights and freedoms of citizens is called the Bill of Rights and _____.
fib.explanation: It is officially the Bill of Rights and Duties, covering both citizens' rights and their fundamental obligations.

fib.questionText: The national institution in Tanzania abbreviated as CHRAGG stands for the Commission for Human Rights and Good _____.
fib.explanation: CHRAGG is the Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance.

fib.questionText: The characteristic of human rights meaning that they apply to all people everywhere is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Universality means human rights are enjoyed by everyone, without discrimination.

fib.questionText: The right to vote and the right to a fair trial are classified as civil and _____ rights.
fib.explanation: These belong to the category of civil and political rights, which protect freedom and participation in public life.

fib.questionText: The fair distribution of resources, opportunities and privileges in a society is called social _____.
fib.explanation: Social justice is the principle of fairness in the way a society shares its benefits and burdens.

fib.questionText: The Tanzanian law that consolidates the rights and welfare of children is the Law of the _____ Act of 2009.
fib.explanation: The Law of the Child Act, 2009 protects children's rights in Tanzania.

fib.questionText: Giving each person what they need so that everyone can reach a fair outcome describes the concept of _____.
fib.explanation: Equity provides support according to need, unlike equality which treats everyone identically.

fib.questionText: Rights enjoyed collectively, such as the right to development and a clean environment, are known as group or _____ rights.
fib.explanation: Group or solidarity rights are third-generation rights enjoyed by communities together.

tf.questionText: Human rights belong to a person from birth and do not have to be earned.
tf.explanation: Human rights are inherent; every person possesses them simply by being human.

tf.questionText: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is a legally binding treaty that every country must obey by force of law.
tf.explanation: The UDHR is a declaration setting a common standard; it is not itself a binding treaty, although many of its principles are reflected in binding instruments and national laws.

tf.questionText: The Bill of Rights was added to the Constitution of Tanzania in 1984.
tf.explanation: The Bill of Rights and Duties was incorporated into the Constitution through the Fifth Constitutional Amendment in 1984.

tf.questionText: Enjoying your rights means you have no responsibility to respect the rights of other people.
tf.explanation: Rights and responsibilities go together; everyone must respect the equal rights of others.

tf.questionText: CHRAGG can investigate complaints about violations of human rights in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: The Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance receives and investigates complaints of human rights violations and maladministration.

tf.questionText: Equality and equity mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: Equality means treating everyone the same, while equity means giving each person what they need for a fair outcome.

tf.questionText: Persons with disabilities have special legal protection of their rights in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Tanzania has laws such as the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2010 that protect the rights and welfare of persons with disabilities.

tf.questionText: Poverty and ignorance of rights can contribute to human rights violations.
tf.explanation: Poverty, ignorance, discrimination and weak law enforcement are among the main causes of human rights abuses.

tf.questionText: Child labour that denies a child the right to education is a violation of human rights.
tf.explanation: Exploitative child labour violates children's rights to education, protection and development.

tf.questionText: Civil society organisations and the courts have no role in protecting human rights in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Courts, CHRAGG, civil society organisations and human rights education all play important roles in protecting and promoting human rights.

summary.questionText: State the meaning of human rights.
summary.correctAnswer: Human rights are the basic entitlements and freedoms that belong to every person from birth simply because they are human, regardless of race, sex, religion, status or nationality.
summary.explanation: This captures the inherent and universal nature of human rights.

summary.questionText: Mention three main characteristics of human rights.
summary.correctAnswer: Human rights are universal (they apply to everyone everywhere), inalienable (they cannot be taken away or surrendered) and indivisible (all rights are equally important and interconnected).
summary.explanation: Universality, inalienability and indivisibility are the core characteristics tested at this level.

summary.questionText: Identify the three main categories of human rights.
summary.correctAnswer: The three categories are civil and political rights (such as the right to vote and a fair trial); economic, social and cultural rights (such as the rights to education, health and work); and group or solidarity rights (such as the rights to development, peace and a clean environment).
summary.explanation: These correspond to the three generations of human rights.

summary.questionText: Briefly explain the importance of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948.
summary.correctAnswer: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations in 1948, set a common standard of human rights for all peoples and nations, inspired many national constitutions and international treaties, and became the foundation of modern human rights protection worldwide.
summary.explanation: The UDHR is the foundational global human rights document influencing later instruments and constitutions.

summary.questionText: Explain how human rights are protected in the Constitution of Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: The Constitution of Tanzania protects human rights through the Bill of Rights and Duties, added in 1984, which guarantees basic rights and freedoms such as equality, freedom of expression and the right to life, while also stating the fundamental duties of citizens; these rights can be enforced through the courts.
summary.explanation: Constitutional protection rests on the Bill of Rights and Duties and judicial enforcement.

summary.questionText: State four rights of children that are protected by law in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Children have the rights to a name and nationality, to education, to health care, and to protection from abuse, neglect and exploitative labour, as protected under the Law of the Child Act of 2009.
summary.explanation: These reflect the protections under the Law of the Child Act, 2009.

summary.correctAnswer: Equality means treating all people in the same way and giving them the same resources, while equity means recognising people's different needs and giving each person the support they require so that everyone can achieve a fair outcome.
summary.explanation: Equality is sameness of treatment; equity is fairness adjusted to need.

summary.questionText: Outline three causes of human rights violations in society.
summary.correctAnswer: Human rights violations are caused by factors such as ignorance of one's rights, poverty, discrimination based on sex, tribe or religion, abuse of power by those in authority, and weak enforcement of laws.
summary.explanation: Any three of these recognised causes are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Describe the role of the Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance (CHRAGG) in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: CHRAGG promotes and protects human rights and good governance by educating the public about their rights, receiving and investigating complaints of human rights violations and maladministration, advising the government, and recommending measures to remedy abuses.
summary.explanation: CHRAGG is Tanzania's national human rights institution with education, investigation and advisory functions.

summary.questionText: Explain the relationship between rights and responsibilities.
summary.correctAnswer: Rights and responsibilities are inseparable; while every citizen is entitled to their rights, they also have the responsibility to respect the equal rights of others, obey the law, and contribute to society, so that the enjoyment of rights by one person does not harm the rights of others.
summary.explanation: This highlights the mutual link between enjoying rights and fulfilling duties.

hoq.questionText: A factory owner in Mwanza refuses to pay female workers the same wage as male workers doing identical jobs and does not allow them maternity leave. Which combination of human rights principles is being violated?

options.text: The right to a clean environment and the right to peace
Equality and non-discrimination together with the labour and special rights of women workers
The right to vote and the right to a fair trial
The right to nationality and the right to development

hoq.explanation: Paying women less for equal work and denying maternity leave breaches the principles of equality and non-discrimination as well as the special protection of women's labour rights guaranteed in Tanzanian law and the Constitution.

hoq.questionText: A village leader bars children with disabilities from attending the local primary school, claiming the school has no special facilities. As a citizen who understands human rights, the most appropriate and rights-based response is to

options.text: Agree that the children should simply stay at home until facilities exist
Advocate for inclusive education and report the discrimination to authorities such as CHRAGG, since children with disabilities have an equal right to education
Demand that all other children also be removed from the school
Ignore the matter because education is not a human right

hoq.explanation: Education is a protected right and persons with disabilities are a special group entitled to equal access; the correct response is to promote inclusive education and report the discrimination to a body like CHRAGG, reflecting both equity and the citizen's role in protecting rights.

hoq.questionText: During a public protest, some citizens damage shops and beat a suspected thief without taking him to the police. This situation BEST illustrates which key lesson about human rights and responsibilities?

options.text: That freedom of expression has no limits at all
That exercising one's rights must be balanced with the responsibility to respect others' rights and the rule of law, including the suspect's right to a fair trial
That citizens are allowed to punish suspects themselves
That property owners have no rights during a protest

hoq.explanation: While citizens have the right to assemble and express themselves, they must respect the rights of others and the rule of law; mob justice violates the suspect's right to a fair trial and the property rights of shop owners, showing that rights carry corresponding responsibilities.
